strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing static dataset limitations in agent evaluation through principled knowledge graph-based task generation
Comprehensive system design with clear five-stage pipeline supporting both document comprehension and web interaction tasks across multiple agent types
Practical instantiation with GRAPH2EVAL-BENCH (1,319 tasks) demonstrating scalability with measured efficiency metrics (34.87s per doc task, 95.51s per web task)
Extensive empirical evaluation across 7+ models using multiple metrics (F1, ROUGE-L, LLM-Judge, Success Rate) showing effective performance differentiation
First framework for automatically generating interactive web-based agent tasks, representing novel contribution to the field
Clear presentation with well-structured workflows, effective visualizations, and detailed appendices
Broad experimental coverage including single-agent, multi-agent, SoM, and Agent S 2.5 configurations with models of varying scales
weaknesses: Evaluation methodology relies heavily on LLM-as-a-judge without inter-annotator agreement validation, confidence intervals, or evidence of evaluator consistency; no human evaluation of task quality provided

Critical experimental findings unexplained: multi-agent collaboration shows no improvement over single agents while increasing token usage (contradicting design rationale), and web task success rates collapse (~14% for SoM Agent) without root cause analysis

Limited technical novelty in individual components: KG construction uses standard definitions, subgraph sampling applies straightforward techniques (cosine similarity, k-hop neighborhoods), task generation relies on LLM prompting, and coverage optimization uses standard MMR

Missing ablation studies for key components (sampling strategies, filtering stages, template constraints); no comparison with cited baselines (TaskCraft, Zhang et al. 2025); no significance testing, confidence intervals, or statistical rigor
Knowledge graph construction under-specified: entity/relation extraction quality not evaluated, visual-to-text conversion not detailed, no analysis of information loss or extraction errors

Generalization concerns: small data sources (16 documents + 8 websites), narrow domain representation (research-heavy), no cross-domain or held-out test evaluation; unclear scalability to diverse document types beyond academic papers

Web interaction portion under-developed: only 317 tasks (24% of total) with narrow type distribution (58% are business_search_filter); poor absolute performance unexplained; safety task generation preliminary and not integrated

Reproducibility issues: code availability claim appears malformed ('available here: gpt-4o'), key hyperparameters lack justification (τ threshold, k-hop distance), heavy dependence on proprietary models

strengths: Addresses important problem: Automatic scalable task generation for agent evaluation avoids memorization bias of static datasets
Comprehensive systems design: Complete pipeline from data parsing through coverage optimization with principled stages
Multimodal and multi-scenario support: Handles both document comprehension and web interaction systematically, with multiple agent architectures
Practical implementation demonstrating feasibility: GRAPH2EVAL-BENCH with 1,319 tasks generated efficiently (34.87s per document task)
Broad experimental validation: Evaluation across 7+ models shows tasks effectively differentiate performance across agent-model combinations
Clear presentation: Well-structured paper with informative figures and logical flow
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Individual components (embeddings, subgraph sampling, LLM generation) are standard; primary contribution is engineering integration rather than methodological innovation
Insufficient task quality validation: No human evaluation of generated tasks; limited empirical analysis beyond filtering stages; no quality metrics or examples in main text demonstrating diversity
Lack of comparison with existing benchmarks: No empirical comparison with Mind2Web, WebArena, or GAIA; advantages over existing approaches not quantitatively validated
Concerning experimental results: Web task success rates very low (14.51% for SoM Agent on Gemini); multi-agent shows no improvement or degradation on documents—neither phenomenon adequately analyzed

Evaluation methodology limitations: F1/ROUGE-L insufficient for semantic understanding; LLM-as-judge introduces bias with no consistency analysis; binary success metric for web tasks is coarse-grained without error analysis
Missing ablation studies: No ablations on filtering stages, sampling strategies, template design, or knowledge graph choices; relative contributions unclear
Limited dataset scope: Only 16 documents and 8 websites as sources; potential data contamination with model training data not discussed; 1,319 tasks is modest compared to some benchmarks

Insufficient technical clarity: Subgraph sampling strategy abstractly described; meta-path design process unclear and appears to require manual specification; coverage optimization rationale not justified
Limited analysis of results: No investigation into failure modes, task difficulty calibration, whether tasks are representative of real challenges, or what performance patterns actually measure

strengths: Addresses important problem: static evaluation sets cannot distinguish true agent generalization from memorization; scalable task generation is critical
Thoughtful framework design: five-stage pipeline elegantly decomposes the problem; using KGs to model entity relationships explicitly is more principled than LLM-only generation

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: multiple agent types (Single/Multi-Agent for RAG; SoM/Agent S 2.5 for web), diverse LLMs (GPT, Deepseek, Qwen, Gemini), multiple metrics (F1, ROUGE-L, LLM-as-Judge), human validation (88% agreement on 50 web tasks)
Dual-scenario support: unified framework for both document understanding and web interaction tasks demonstrates good generality with appropriate scenario-specific strategies
Strong empirical improvements: 20% semantic consistency gain and 17% solvability improvement over KG-free baseline with 88% KG Edge Precision validation
Reproducibility and completeness: extensive appendices covering task templates, meta-paths, agent architectures, metrics, safety considerations, and implementation details facilitate reproduction
Useful dataset contribution: Graph2Eval-Bench with 1,319 tasks spanning document understanding and web interaction will be valuable for the agent evaluation community
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: individual components use standard techniques (semantic chunking, embedding search, LLM prompting with templates); contribution is primarily in orchestration rather than novel algorithms

Weak baseline comparisons: KG-free variant is authors' own ablation not published methods; TaskCraft comparison (Table 6) is qualitative without quantitative metrics on identical tasks; missing comparisons with Su et al. [31] and other recent synthetic generation methods; no direct quality comparison against human-written tasks

Insufficient KG validation: KG Edge Precision validated on only 100 pairs across two data sources (88% means 12% error); no analysis of how KG errors propagate to task quality; dependency on accurate graph modeling is critical but not thoroughly validated

Web task performance raises quality concerns: SoM Agent 14.51% and Agent S 2.5 69.20% success rates lack error analysis; unclear whether tasks are unreasonably difficult, poorly specified, or reveal genuine agent limitations; no systematic failure mode categorization

Evaluation metric limitations: LLM-as-a-Judge is subjective for document tasks; LLM evaluation of dynamic web states is error-prone; metric validation limited to 50 samples; missing inter-annotator agreement statistics (Cohen's κ, Krippendorff's α)
Incomplete failure analysis: limited analysis of task generation failures; only brief case study; no systematic categorization of error types or analysis of semantic inconsistency occurrence rates

Unbalanced task distribution: web tasks heavily skewed toward business_search_filter (61% of tasks); limited analysis of coverage uniformity and whether this reflects real-world use or generation bias

Scalability and practical concerns: task generation requires 34.87s per document and 95.51s per web task (costly at scale); no discussion of computational requirements; web tasks rely on live crawling limiting reproducibility; unclear snapshot management for long-term stability

Safety and privacy handling is ad-hoc: Appendix A filtering lacks validation; business data placeholder mechanism mentioned but not validated; potential privacy leakage in web crawling; no clear audit trail for sensitive information removal

Insufficient ablation studies: no ablation on individual filtering stages, alternative sampling strategies, or hyperparameter sensitivity (similarity threshold τ, hop distance k appear empirically chosen); meta-path design priority strategy lacks principled justification

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing genuine limitations of static agent evaluation datasets with clear articulation of challenges in semantic consistency and solvability

Comprehensive end-to-end framework with thoughtful pipeline design (data ingestion → KG construction → subgraph sampling → task generation → coverage optimization) that unifies document understanding and web interaction tasks
Extensive experimental evaluation across 4 agent types, 8+ model families, multiple metrics, with ablation studies and human validation (88% agreement with GPT-4o on 50 samples)
Practical contribution: GRAPH2EVAL-BENCH dataset with 1,319 tasks showing improvements of 20% in semantic consistency and 17% in solvability over KG-free baseline
Strong reproducibility with detailed appendices covering agent architectures, task templates, meta-paths, metrics formulas, and implementation details
Safety considerations integrated for both document and web tasks with explicit privacy and content safety constraints
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: framework primarily combines existing techniques (KG construction, embedding-based retrieval, subgraph sampling, LLM generation) with novelty in application rather than methodology; Algorithm 1 is straightforward

Weak baseline comparisons: KG-free baseline is authors' own method without KG structure; only qualitative comparison with TaskCraft; missing quantitative evaluations on same dataset against other recent synthetic task generation methods

Web task evaluation underdeveloped: only 317 web tasks from 8 websites (vs. 1,002 document tasks from 16 documents) with very low success rates (14.51% SoM Agent, 69.20% Agent S 2.5), raising concerns about task quality calibration and potential alignment to specific agent capabilities

Knowledge graph robustness underexplored: 88% KG Edge Precision acknowledged but no systematic analysis of how 12% error rate impacts task quality; limited mitigation strategies for KG incompleteness or errors despite acknowledged reliance on accurate modeling

Insufficient task diversity evaluation: diversity claims lack quantitative support; MMR-based selection mentioned but not thoroughly evaluated; no systematic analysis of coverage dimensions (node type, edge type, pattern) translating to meaningful task diversity

Scalability concerns unaddressed: generation costs 34.87s/document task and 95.51s/web task requiring GPT-4o; no computational cost analysis or discussion of barriers to large-scale adoption; economic constraints unclear

Underspecified critical components: visual-to-text conversion function ϕ_visual not detailed; different subgraph sampling strategies listed but not quantitatively compared; variable extraction process barely discussed; specific E_web relation types not fully enumerated

Human evaluation limitations: only 1,000 tasks with 2 annotators; no inter-annotator agreement scores; document web tasks show only 78%/72% consistency/solvability but no analysis of causes for 22-28% unsolvable tasks or failure case patterns
Safety task generation (Appendix I) appears preliminary with no evaluation results; unclear whether included in the 1,319 tasks; underdeveloped contribution claiming to improve robustness evaluation

Presentation issues: critical details relegated to appendices making main paper dense; relationships between concepts (document understanding, RAG agents, knowledge retrieval) could be clearer; missing code/data availability statement and project page URL
